week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent.

new.description: A dreamy underwater world you can swim through in your browser: swaying kelp forests, sunbeams, a sunken ship and manta rays. Everything is generated by code with WebGPU (no images, models or sound files), all in a single 97 KB HTML file.
new.readme: A dreamy underwater world you can swim through, right in your browser. Towering kelp forests, sunbeams pouring through a rippling surface, a sunken ship, manta rays gliding overhead. new.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
new.readme: An agent skill for hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: single-user and concurrent decode startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: Compute the theoretical ceiling. Measure against interleaved controls. Log every result, including the failures. Gate on long-context retrieval.

It’s variable in weight and roundness, with proportions and curves designed to feel warm without being too cute and clear without being too cold. It’s a perfect companion out of the box, and three variable axes and plenty of alternates let you tune its personality to exactly what you need. Allo is optimized for screens and interfaces, with an optical size that adjusts automatically between text and display.

new.description: AI clipping for long videos and live streams. Self-hosted, bring your own AI key.
new.readme: Turn long videos and live streams into captioned vertical clips, ready to post. Free and open source: run it on your own computer or server, with your own AI key. Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to 9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. gap.method: Lag is how long before the open model's release a closed model first reached the same Capabilities Index score. Today's figure measures from that closed model to today, so it grows until an open model moves the frontier.

hardware.finding: GeForce RTX 5090 decodes fastest; DGX Spark fits the biggest models

possibilities.title: Remote Claude Code fleets in AWS get a learning loop that lowers cost
possibilities.why: Claude Code on Bedrock AgentCore runs isolated remote sessions with no cost figures, and TokenEconomizer learns from repository sessions to cut cost, so a fleet working the same repositories feeds the plugin more sessions to learn from.

possibilities.title: On-call engineers can question a whole incident's logs in a single context
possibilities.why: Headroom compresses logs and JSON before the model sees them, and Qwen4-Max holds 1 million tokens at $1.50 per million input tokens with measured lower task costs, so an entire incident window can fit cheaply.

possibilities.title: Analysts in regulated firms can query private databases with a 321B-class model on one desk
possibilities.why: The 2.48 bpw quants put a 321B-class MoE on one DGX Spark, datasette-llm can call any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and llama.cpp's new slot scheduler and prompt hashing target exactly this kind of shared local server.

possibilities.title: QA teams can let Codex debug internal staging sites without exposing them
possibilities.why: Chrome DevTools MCP is becoming a standard agent tool for browser debugging, and OpenAI's secure tunnel connects private or localhost MCP servers to Codex without a public endpoint, so a DevTools server inside the network can serve a cloud agent.

possibilities.title: Shared agent skills become dependable team standards once they survive compaction
possibilities.why: Matt Pocock's agent skills show demand for shared skills, and Kiro now reloads requested skills after compaction and lets users set when compaction starts, so a team skill no longer silently drops out of long runs.
